title: Latency Budget Collaboration Charter and Rollout Plan
content:
Purpose:

This is a working charter for establishing latency budgets for Redwood Inference services and a cross-functional plan to operationalize them. The focus is practical: define service-level latency targets, map owner responsibilities, create lightweight telemetry and alerting, and embed latency awareness into the cadence of product and platform teams.

Scope:
- Core inference endpoints (text-generation API, embedding service) and the Console API routes used by product-facing dashboards.
- Initial scope covers p50/p95/p99 buckets for user-facing request paths; downstream work will cover RPCs between microservices.
- Excluded: batch jobs, nightly maintenance windows, ad-hoc admin tooling.

Goals (near-term, 90 days):
1) Agree on latency budgeting model and measurable definitions for p50/p95/p99 per route.
2) Instrument baseline telemetry for the top 12 routes (by request volume) and publish a first-month baseline report.
3) Create routing-aware alerts tied to latency budget burn (error-budget-like workflows for latency).
4) Pilot rollout with Hosted-API team and one Dedicated-inference pool to validate cross-deploy behavior.

Why this matters:
- Latency is a primary product-quality vector for our customers; setting budgets forces explicit trade-offs (cost vs latency vs availability).
- A shared budget and response plan reduces firefighting friction between product, infra, and SRE when latency regresses.

Definitions:
- Latency budget: an agreed permissible tail latency for a given route (example: p95 < 300ms for token-generation-init).
- Budget burn: the fraction of time window where observed latency exceeds target.
- Action threshold: burn% that triggers a coordinated response (suggested: 5% burn over rolling 1h triggers investigation; 20% burn triggers mitigation/escalation).

Stakeholders and primary points of contact:
- Eng-SRE (lead): Aisha Patel (owner) — charter sponsor, runbook authoring, oncall integration.
- Hosted API/Product: Marcus Liu — route owners, rollback/run rollout authority.
- Serving Runtime: Sophie Nguyen — kernel/quantization mitigations, batching config changes.
- Observability/Monitoring: Diego Ramirez — dashboards, derived metrics, alert plumbing.
- Solutions/Support: Priya Shah — customer-impact assessment and comms.
- Engineering managers for Pilot teams: assigned per squad.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Visibility: dashboards for top 12 routes live and accessible to stakeholders within 3 weeks.
- Baseline reduction: average p95 improvement goal of 10–20% across pilot routes after runbook optimizations.
- Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for latency incidents reduced by 30% vs baseline.
- Number of rollouts that include a latency impact assessment increased to 90% for feature releases in pilot teams.

Proposed latency budget examples (pilot targets — concrete but negotiable):
- Text-generation token service (init token latency): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms.
- Streaming token delivery (per-token): p50 < 10ms, p95 < 50ms.
- Embeddings vectorize route: p50 < 70ms, p95 < 250ms.
- Console list/endpoints: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 500ms.
Note: these numbers are placeholders. Instrumentation will confirm realistic targets per model family and sequence lengths.

Telemetry and instrumentation plan:
- Instrumentation owner: Diego. Implement histograms for request durations with labels: route, model_family, sequence_len_bucket, deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private), region.
- Data retention: 30d raw, 90d rolled-up.
- Alerts: two-tier alerts — advisory (burn > 5% in 1h) and critical (burn > 20% in 15m). Advisory goes to priority Slack channel and the owning team, critical pages SRE oncall and product+runtime leads.
- Dashboards: route-level summary, cohort drilldowns (model, seq_len), and an index of routes by contribution to tail-latency.

Runbooks and playbooks:
- Create light-weight runbooks per route with: quick inspection queries, mitigation knobs (reduce batch_size, failover to lower-cost model variant, enable caching), and communication templates.
- Example mitigation flow: detect burn -> run quick diagnostic query -> take mitigation (route config change or model fallback) -> monitor -> roll back and investigate.
- Keep mitigations small and reversible; avoid sweeping infra changes during customer-impacting events.

Cross-functional cadence and rituals:
- Weekly 30m sync during pilot with SRE + Hosted API + Serving Runtime + Observability. Agenda: data review (5m), recent incidents (10m), action items (10m), blockers (5m).
- Monthly latency retrospective with product managers and support to connect regressions to product changes.
- Pre-release checklist addition: new or modified routes require a latency impact note (estimated added p95, tests run against perf harness).

Pilot rollout plan (8 weeks):
Week 0-1: finalize charter and targets, align pilot teams, and get instrumentation sprint booked.
Week 2-3: implement histograms and dashboards for top 12 routes; smoke test alerts.
Week 4: collect baseline metrics and publish first baseline report.
Week 5-6: iterate on runbooks, implement 2 common mitigations (model fallback and batching tweaks).
Week 7: fire drill — simulate a 25% traffic increase and test mitigation procedures.
Week 8: evaluate pilot, gather feedback, and decide next-stage rollout to Dedicated and Private deployments.

RACI (simple):
- Define budgets: Product + SRE (Responsible: Product owner, Accountable: SRE lead).
- Instrument metrics: Observability (Responsible), SRE (Consulted).
- Create runbooks: SRE (Responsible), Runtime (Consulted).
- Mitigations in prod: Route owner (Responsible), SRE (Consulted), Runtime (Support).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Metrics noise from small-volume routes leading to false alarms. Mitigation: prioritize high-volume routes for automation; add minimum-sample thresholds.
- Risk: Conflicting priorities (cost vs latency) across teams. Mitigation: create a decision rubric that quantifies cost per ms and presents trade-offs.
- Risk: Overly aggressive mitigation causing availability regressions. Mitigation: require canaryed mitigation and automatic rollback thresholds.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Agree final action thresholds (5%/20% are suggestions).
- Decide whether latency budgets should be enforced per-model-variant or per-route only.
- Policy for customer-facing SLAs vs internal budgets (how to expose/communicate).

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Diego: spin up histograms for the 12 top routes and share dashboard link. (Due: 2026-03-12)
- Marcus: confirm list of pilot routes and assign route owners. (Due: 2026-03-09)
- Sophie: draft two mitigation knobs with runbook snippets (batch size, fallback model variant). (Due: 2026-03-15)
- Aisha: publish charter to Confluence and schedule weekly pilot sync. (Due: 2026-03-08)

Appendix: Notes from previous experiments and references:
- Prior latency experiments in infra repo: /github/infra/latency-bench (see PR #8 for batching analysis).
- Related Jira: SRV-4821 (investigate p99 spikes during load) and SRV-4867 (streaming improvements).
- Slack threads: #sre-latency-thread and #hosting-api-deploys for coordination history.

Document status:
- Drafted by Aisha Patel and collaborators. This is an iterative working doc; feedback welcome. After pilot, this will be converted to a short canonical playbook that teams can reference for rollout to Dedicated and Private deployments.
